agent_notes: STEPBible's entity link tags אֲדֹנָי as deity.yhwh. Whether the subject is God at the king's right hand or the king himself (with God's seat on the right in v. 1) is disputed; I kept 'the Lord' (אֲדֹנָי) as God, following the Targum (the Shekhinah of the LORD) and Rashi.

The line has several cruxes: מָלֵא גְוִיּוֹת has no stated object (KJV 'fills the places' supplies one, ASV the same); רֹאשׁ may be singular ('a head') or collective ('heads'); אֶרֶץ רַבָּה is 'a wide land' or 'many lands'. I kept the Hebrew singulars in the literal layer.

Verb tenses throughout (מָחַץ in 5 and 6 perfect, the rest imperfect) are read as prophetic perfects mixed with future imperfects. I kept the Hebrew tenses in the literal layer and unified them in the dramatic layer, as Ibn Ezra explains the perfects as a standing, timeless fact.
